To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the renal shift table analysis of telavancini and vancomycin-treated patients in phase III clinical trials showed no significant differences in the incidence of renal impairment, but the incidence of acute kidney injury (AKI) was higher with telavancin than with vancomycin.

telavancin is associated with a lower incidence of renal dysfunction than vancomycin, as measured by the incidence of serum creatinine increases of 0.5 mg/dL, 1.0 mg/dL and 2.0 mg/mL, as well as by the incidence of acute kidney injury, as measured by increases in serum creatinine of >1.5 mg/mL and >1.0 × baseline serum creatinine.
telavancin is not inferior to vancomycin in terms of renal function changes in patients with S aureus HAP or VABP.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of novel methods of analysis of time course and extent of changes of renal function in patients treated with antibiotics for pneumonia, and the development of new methods of treatment for patients suffering from pneumonia.
the development of novel and effective antimicrobial agents.
the development of new methods for the treatment of patients with chronic renal disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
telavancin was not associated with more renal toxicity than vancomycin.
telavancin is not superior to vancomycin in the treatment of patients with Staphylococcusaureusbacteremia.
telavancin is a reasonable alternative to vancomycin for the treatment of Staphylococcusal pneumonias.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
telavancin and the vancomycin comparator had similar renal function changes in the ATTAIN trials.
telavancin was associated with less renal function decline and a lower incidence of acute renal failure compared with vancomycin.
renal shift table analysis is an effective way to assess renal changes in patients treated with telavancin and/or vancomycin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
telavancin is associated with a significantly lower incidence of clinically significant renal impairment compared with vancomycin.
telavancin is associated with a lower rate of renal function changes, and that the rate of renal function change is similar between telavancin and linezolid.
telavancin and standard of care vancomycin are associated with similar renal toxicity, and the extent and time course of renal function changes are comparable for both agents.
